UCDP documents the Ron-Kulere dyad in Bokkos through August. A December 1 report identifies a local group of assailants and a Fulani victim in Bokkos, but does not verify the assailants as the exact Ron-Kulere armed actor. Do not infer identity from the local government's territory.

Independent December field reporting identifies Petaka in the JNIM–Dozo clash area, a FIDH investigation associates the Petaka post with Dan Na Ambassagou, and December SIPRI research documents the continuing rivalry. The conflict remains local to central Mali.

The Brazilian Forum on Public Security’s 2025 field research describes the expansion of Comando Vermelho and increased conflict with regional factions including Bonde dos 40. A federal justice ministry planning document independently describes the current Maranhão dispute between these named groups. Localized non-state conflict in Maranhão at medium confidence.

Brazilian Public Security Forum fieldwork documents a continuing B40–PCC rivalry in eastern Maranhão. A December 31 killing in Teresina was later attributed by police to a suspected PCC operative and a B40-linked target. Earlier reporting differed about the affiliation of other suspects. This establishes a localized armed rivalry with qualified attribution. The simulation does not assign either faction territorial control.

Model a localized non-state conflict without assigning entire provinces as faction territory.

UCDP's coding and an April report support a rivalry between Benue militias, including a reported response attributed to a commander called Full Fire. Competing contemporary accounts attribute the deaths differently. Broader regional insecurity does not independently establish continuing Chain Guys–Full Force fighting on 1 January.

UNMISS documented attacks by armed Murle elements against Toposa communities in Q2 and attacks by armed Toposa elements against Murle communities in Q3. The April reconciliation pledge did not end violence. Another exact incident took place in February 2026. The available record does not settle January 1 status.

Police-sourced December reporting explicitly names an ongoing Los Lobos–Sao Box rivalry in El Oro. Later December local reporting corroborates the Sao Box faction’s presence and serious violence. Its reporting does not independently establish the identity of the opposing attacker in that later incident. Sao Box is a Los Lobos splinter and is called Los Lobos Box in the source catalog.

Medium-confidence inference of a continuing local conflict in Guayas. Ecuadorian police named the Fénix–Igualitos rivalry in earlier fighting, UCDP records the exact pairing through November 30, the December EUAA assessment identifies the split, and Ecuadorian police still recorded Fénix activity in December. The December record does not independently attribute new bilateral fighting.

The Secretary-General's report documents the January Magwi attack by Murle and Acholi armed elements against Bor herders. A February 13 local consultation agreed on cattle withdrawal and an investigation. Those measures do not establish a ceasefire signed by all three exact parties or a continued organized front in December.

The Fulani and Ngambaye parties signed the Mandakao reconciliation agreement on 5 July to end the specific Logone Occidental episode. The national human rights commission records the accord. Keep it as a concluded local conflict with reconciliation measures, distinct from violence elsewhere in Chad.

The African Union documented the Ethiopian government's December agreement with the Amhara Fano Popular Organization. It does not establish the status of the distinct clash between the Amhara Fano National Force and AFPO. Do not assign the government's agreement to the non-state pair.

Ghana's government reported restored calm after the August Gbinyiri episode and began mediation. UNICEF reports most displaced people had returned by the end of September. Treat the acute hostilities as concluded while the land dispute and government-led mediation remained unresolved on 1 January.

The August Luac-Jang–Jalwau peace commitments did not hold throughout the period. Monitoring records suspected Jalwau-linked violence against Luac-Jang on 26 November and a further incident against Luac-Jang in the same area on 27 December with unidentified perpetrators. The evidence supports continuing local violence after the commitments. Pan-Juaj participated earlier and Warrap authorities reported its return and reconciliation in August, so its involvement on 1 January is unverified.

Yakuman and Yangukun agreed to a local peace framework in Enga on November 21. Police reported early violations. December 5 police-sourced reporting says Yakuman had ceased fighting under the agreement. Represent an imperfect ceasefire framework with continued monitoring, at medium confidence.

The UN identified a November 4 armed clash between Boulala and Kreda elements. Chadian authorities called for mediation immediately afterward. December evidence does not establish a second exact event or an implemented ceasefire.

The recorded Sudanese armed factions' alignment changed in 2025, and the neutral protection formation changed its position. Evidence for those shifts and for the broader civil war does not establish ongoing combat between the exact organizations.

September reporting identifies Mushere communities in the Bokkos violence. A December incident in Tenti identifies the area but does not identify the exact armed Mushere and Fulani participants. The named December evidence is insufficient to carry the exact dyad into the campaign.

The broader intercommunal violence in Taraba was ongoing. The December army report concerns government operations against unidentified armed groups and does not identify the two armed communities in the candidate dyad.

The UN documents the July communal fighting and a multi-party ceasefire. December incidents document state–National Guard or internal Druze friction and do not confirm an ongoing exact tribal matchup. The documented Syrian government–Suwayda National Guard front is represented separately.

The UN documents the July communal fighting and a multi-party ceasefire. December incidents document state–National Guard or internal Druze friction and do not confirm an ongoing exact tribal matchup. The documented Syrian government–Suwayda National Guard front is represented separately.

The October agreement at Todonyang and Lotira covered local cross-border security. November reporting of renewed violence elsewhere on the border involves the same communities. The December parliamentary record supports persistent border insecurity but does not verify ongoing organized combat or a ceasefire covering the exact dyad throughout the area.

Independent year-end reporting documents continuing violence in Barkin Ladi and Jos South on 16 and 31 December. It records residents' attribution to Fulani armed groups, and a local retrospective reports suspected Berom armed reprisals in December. Represent local armed networks and allow for contested attribution, without assigning combatant status to ethnic communities.

December reports describe insecurity and armed banditry in Zamfara, while field research documents local armed group structures. The identifiable December evidence does not establish that the exact Bungudu group pairing remained active.

UN Group of Experts report S/2025/858 paragraphs 14, 36–38 and 48 document Rwanda Defence Force combat against FDLR elements alongside other parties in eastern DRC, including renewed clashes from October. Paragraph 39 separately names FDLR splinter RUD-Urunana. Represent this as a cross-border non-state conflict in DRC, with Rwanda as a belligerent.

decisions.note: Pakistan’s official statement attributed the December 19 event to the Hafiz Gul Bahadur group. The EUAA identifies that group as leader of the Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan umbrella, and UCDP also codes that December event under the existing IMP relationship. Retain the HGB actor’s identity and roll the documented cutoff activity into the active IMP row. Keep the TTP relationship separate.

In December Jaish al-Adl joined the newly announced Mobarizoun Popular Front, also called the Popular Fighters Front. The front publicly claimed recent fighting in Sistan and Baluchestan that state media independently reported, though the claim of responsibility remains an attribution. Carry the continuing relationship as medium confidence and display the umbrella with the historic faction name. The front’s December manifesto is a declared program.

The Indian government listed a specific NSCN(K) organization in September. December reporting separately records ULFA-I activity. Neither establishes a coordinated operation by the UNLFW umbrella at the cutoff, and the named factions' separate ceasefires and organization sizes cannot be transferred to the umbrella.

Year-end reporting documents fighting across the existing southern fronts alongside the separate PLC–STC clash. The Geneva Academy identifies the STC and PLC as independent participants in fighting Ansar Allah. Represent the southern front as regional and keep its forces separate.
The Iván Mordisco faction announced a unilateral holiday suspension through 7 January. The statement does not extend to the separate EMC splinter or third-party fronts.
The Oman-mediated agreement applied to the United States and the Sana’a authorities. The United Kingdom took part in earlier operations and is not a party to this ceasefire.

The ACLED period report around January 1 notes disputed attribution of a mine incident linked in some accounts to Naparama. Continued mobilization is better evidenced than direct combat with state forces by the cutoff. The Islamic State Mozambique front is tracked separately.
The Geneva Academy dates the end of 2025 Israel–Ansar Allah hostilities to the October Gaza ceasefire. This relationship is absent from the opening roster.

The UN Secretary-General reports December 5 government operations against remaining CMSPR elements in Ouham. UCDP independently identifies the exact government–CMSPR dyad as active again in December, following earlier attacks documented by UN monitors. Geneva Academy classifies the attacks as sporadic and below the legal threshold for a non-international armed conflict. PPO models this armed relationship locally in Ouham.
